subject: hoverPickup
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: militarized pickup converted to hover thrusters.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk.
reasoning:
I'm planning a static pickup-truck-like vehicle model, around 5.4m long and 2m wide, using four thruster pods in place of wheels to give it a hovering look while keeping the lowest points near the floor.

I'll build the body with box geometries for the chassis, cab, bed, and hood, plus ducted-fan-style thruster pods with glowing cyan discs and small landing skids touching the ground. I'm planning SVG textures for headlights, decals, warning stripes, and a HUD screen, along with layered paint schemes like brushed metal panels and mottled dark camo.

Still defining cab geometry...

I'm checking that the glass profile stays inset from the sloped front edge so it doesn't poke through, then setting up a separate windshield plane angled along that slope with its own normal and offset so it sits flush against the cab.

Now moving to the truck bed: adding floor, side wall, and tailgate boxes with dimensions set to match the cab width, plus a bulkhead behind the cab, and considering adding a pintle gun turret mount with pedestal, ring, and dual barrels for the military look.

I need to work out barrel placement so the turret doesn't clash with the cab roof, testing heights and depths until the barrels clear the roofline, which may mean raising the turret on a taller mount instead.

I'm also considering adding missile pods mounted on the bed rails, tilted outward, alongside a roof light bar and antenna array for extra detail. For thrusters, I'll place four pods symmetrically at the front and back corners of the chassis, sitting low near the body.

Each pod needs a mounting pylon connecting it to the chassis, plus a lathed duct ring shell giving it a rounded nozzle silhouette. I'll add a downward-facing fan disc with a glowing cyan blade texture and a small glow ring for engine effect, keep an exhaust cone minimal rather than reaching the floor, and finish with small landing skid legs touching down at y=0 under each pod.

I'm reworking pod placement to avoid overlapping the chassis underside — shifting pods outward to x ±1.3 with a slightly smaller radius so their top edge clears the hull, and adjusting where the pylon attaches at the body's center.

Now I'm thinking through small landing feet for the pods, considering simple strut options like thin spoke legs or small boxes beneath each duct to keep the model grounded.

Adding fan discs glowing cyan inside the ducts visible from above and below, plus neon underglow strips along the sills. Now I'm placing a reinforced front bull bar with grille and glowing headlight bars on the hood.

Separating the front face into an unlit textured grille plane with dark slats and a magenta chevron, plus two glowing ice-white headlight boxes and a magenta DRL strip, along with red taillight glow boxes at the tailgate. Moving on to door line details and number decals.

Still working out decal placement and orientation...

Now I'm planning fender flares, exhaust stacks or intake pipes along the cab sides, and roof details like the light bar, antenna, sensor dish, and roof rack. Estimating around 150 parts total with textures for windshield streak, grille, door emblem, hood stencil, fan blades, plate lettering, and license plate, then starting on the hull paint with a mottled color scheme.

Setting up darker armor plate tones with magenta and cyan accents, planning glow and clockwork imports for metal and panelled materials, and defining a helper function for creating boxes...

Now I'm designing a glowing box variant and a pod-building function that constructs lathed duct shapes with a layered profile along the axis, positioned using scaled offsets.

I'm adding spinning fan discs with glowing textures facing up and down, a magenta glow torus ring around the pod, and a connecting pylon rod linking each pod back to the chassis.

Now I'm sketching in structural details: angled struts front and back of the pod, a fender flare plate over the top, and a wing-stub thruster pylon cover with magenta edging, keeping the intake grill minimal to avoid overcomplicating the model.

Moving on to the chassis underside, I'm adding blocky battery and drive packs plus cyan glow strips along each side below the sill, then thinking through side mirror pods on the cab and a hazard-striped bull bar using alternating yellow and black stripe patterns along the x-axis.

For the rear, I'm placing a tailgate with tail light strip, plate, and glowing magenta plasma vent cylinders under the bed. In the bed itself I'm positioning cargo elements -- striped fuel barrels as cylinders and an ammo crate box -- spaced around the central turret pedestal so nothing overlaps.

Now I'm designing the turret: a pedestal cylinder rising from the bed with brace rods, a ring collar, a gun block box on top, and two barrel cylinders extending outward along the z-axis with the correct radius and spacing so they clear the roof height.

Next I'm adding muzzle brakes as wider short cylinders at the barrel tips, a shield plate box in front with slots for the barrels, and an ammo belt box on the side. I'm also placing rocket pod boxes on each side wall at a height just above the wall's top surface, flanking the pedestal, with a decal texture for the pod's hole pattern on the front face.

Dropping the interior idea since glass is opaque anyway, I'll instead give the glass a lighter tint with reflection streaks. For the cab doors, I'm planning a shared texture with seam lines, an emblem, a stripe, and a number, sized to fit the cab's side panels.

I'm working out the orientation math for mapping this door texture correctly onto the plane depending on which side of the truck the viewer sees.

Working through the remaining panel orientations now: grille and rear plate planes with simple forward/backward facing directions, the rocket pod front, the windshield plane with its tilted normal, and starting to figure out the rear window's sloped geometry at the cab back.

Now I'm placing the rear window glass with a cyan streak texture, then adding hood details—vent slots, a central scoop, and twin magenta neon strips along the hood edges. I'm also sketching out the antenna whip geometry and starting on a dish shape.

Now I'm working out the dish's tilted axis and profile points to create a lathe-generated bowl, then moving on to the roof lightbar with cyan and magenta glowing halves and lens details, followed by armored side sills positioned along the chassis.

I'm adjusting the skirt armor panels to fit within chassis width, then deciding to skip extra intake stacks and cooling fins in favor of simpler neon glow strips along the skirt bottom, and starting on the bed floor and wall geometry.

Now I'm placing the bed floor at the right height and positioning it along the chassis length, then moving to the front bumper with hazard stripes, a bull bar made of vertical rods and a cross piece with a winch cylinder, plus a magenta glowing splitter strip underneath.

Working out the grille plane position relative to the bumper and headlights, sizing the grille narrower so the headlights sit outside it without overlapping, then defining the hood's front face dimensions and extent before moving to the cab front below the windshield.

Now I'm building the hood as a tapered frustum box painted with the hull color, matching the fender pods and wheel hubs already placed. For textures, I'm designing a fan graphic with a dark base circle, cyan rotating blades generated in a loop, and a magenta hub center.

Writing SVG textures...

Adding glowing taillights, plasma exhaust cylinders, and plate positioning on the tailgate...

Setting up mirrors as angled boxes with arm rods connecting to the doors, checking overall height and floor alignment, then defining helper functions for boxes and other geometry to build the rest of the vehicle...

Still working out the glass extrusion placement...

Adding the roof plate position and pod struts as angled rods, then setting up material definitions for the panelled iron armor finish.
